response.title: A Sensor Plan for the Greenhouse
response.passage:
The environmental club at Harbor High planned to use temperature sensors in every bed of its greenhouse before the school science fair. The sensors would help students notice which plants needed extra care. However, several devices stopped working, and the replacement boards had not arrived. Because of the shortage, the club had only six working sensors for ten beds.

Rather than place them wherever they happened to fit, the students checked the greenhouse map and talked with the science teacher. Four beds already held young plants that needed close attention. The other beds would receive seedlings the following week. The club decided to put four sensors beside the young plants and reserve the other two in a cabinet until the new seedlings arrived. That way, the team could use all six devices when they would be most helpful.

The club wrote down its current plan on a board near the greenhouse door: check the four active sensors each morning, keep two in the cabinet, and move them when the seedlings arrive. The teacher explained that the plan could change if the replacement boards came early. The students agreed to update the board if that happened, so everyone would know which devices were in use.

On Monday, the students followed the plan and recorded the readings before class. They found that one bed was warmer than the others, so they opened its window for a short time. The club could not yet monitor every bed, but its notes showed that the limited sensors were being used where they could guide an immediate decision.

items.answer: They kept two sensors in a cabinet until the new seedlings arrived.
distractors: They placed all six sensors beside the young plants right away.
They sent two working sensors back with the delayed replacement boards.
They gave the two extra sensors to another club for the science fair.
items.question: What did the club decide to do with two of its working sensors?

items.answer: The replacement boards had not arrived, leaving the club with fewer working sensors than beds.
distractors: The greenhouse had fewer beds than working sensors, so some devices were unused.
The students had lost the greenhouse map and could not find places for the sensors.
The teacher had asked the club to stop using sensors until after the science fair.
items.question: Why could the club not put a working sensor in every bed?

items.answer: It was the plan the students were following at that time, though it could change.
distractors: It was the plan the club had followed during the previous school year.
It was a final plan that would stay the same even if boards arrived early.
It was a plan that would begin only after all the replacement boards arrived.
